title: Auditable QA metrics suite for FP8/INT8 quantization profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, auditable quality-assurance metrics suite that validates FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles across production workloads. The suite should compute standard metrics (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, Rouge/BLEU) and a set of task-specific scorers (QA, summarization, translation, classification), produce human-readable audit artifacts, and integrate as a gating check before profile rollout. Outputs must include per-task drift diagnostics, confidence intervals, and an explainability summary that maps quality regressions to dataset slices and prompt templates.
acceptance_criteria: A metrics pipeline exists that computes perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, Rouge-1/2/L, BLEU (sacreBLEU), and at least three task-specific scorers (QA F1/EM, summarization Rouge-L, translation BLEU) for a given quant profile run
Each metric run produces a versioned JSON report with per-task breakdowns, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and sample-level delta lists between baseline FP16 and target FP8/INT8
Reports are stored in S3 under s3://redwood-quant-audit/<profile>/<date>/report.json and linked from the validation dashboard
A gating rule (configurable) flags a profile as FAIL when any high-impact task (label=high) drops by >1.5% absolute accuracy or when aggregate quality-index drops by >1.0%
CI job runs execute the metrics suite on a representative smoke dataset within 45 minutes on the dedicated eval fleet and artifacts are archived for 90 days
Dashboard visualizations show per-class confusion matrices, per-prompt prefix delta histograms, and a prioritized regression list for triage
Documentation page (Confluence) with example invocations, expected outputs, and troubleshooting steps is published
design_notes: Rationale: existing quant validation tasks focus on point estimates; we need auditable intervals and sample-level traceability so platform owners can defend rollouts to customers

Metric selection: use perplexity for generative baseline, MMLU-style micro/macro accuracy for reasoning tasks, Rouge/BLEU for summarization/translation, and task-specific scorers implemented as pluggable adapters
Scoring adapters: define a small SDK spec (score(metric_name, reference, candidate, metadata) -> numeric) so downstream users can add custom tasks without changing core pipeline
Statistical testing: prefer bootstrap CIs for non-parametric estimator robustness; use paired tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank) for sample-level comparisons where applicable
Explainability: include top-k prompts where output changed most and a token-level difference view for short-form tasks to aid debugging
Storage schema: flattened JSON report with string fields and arrays only (to match audit ingestion), and artifacts named by profile id and commit hash
Privacy: ensure PII is redacted before storing examples in S3; pipeline must run optional PII-filter step
implementation_plan: Week 1: Define metric adapter SDK, proto tests, and minimal example adapters for QA/summarization/translation (owner: Liam)
Week 2: Implement pipeline runner that executes adapters in parallel on the eval fleet, collects raw outputs, computes metrics and bootstrap CIs (owner: Data Infra)
Week 3: Add delta computation between baseline (FP16) and candidate (FP8/INT8), generate prioritized regression list and sample diffs (owner: Metric Team)
Week 4: Hook pipeline outputs to validation dashboard and S3 storage, add gating rule evaluator and JSON schema validation (owner: Observability)
Week 5: Run end-to-end experiments for 10 representative quant profiles, iterate on thresholds and CI tuning (owner: QA)
Parallel: security and PII redaction integration with KMS and redact library (owner: Security)
Deliverables: metric-adapters lib, pipeline runner, S3 report schema, dashboard panels, CI job config, Confluence doc
validation_plan: Datasets: use MMLU subset (curated 20 tasks), XSum for summarization, WMT minor subset for translation, NaturalQuestions/VizQA slices for QA; include both in-distribution and shifted slices
Baselines: run FP16 baseline and INT8/FP8 candidates; keep identical seeds and prompt templates to ensure comparability
Metrics: compute per-task score, aggregate weighted quality-index (weights configured by product), and per-slice deltas
Stat tests: bootstrap 10k resamples for CI, paired Wilcoxon for per-sample rank changes, and Holm-Bonferroni correction across multiple tasks
Edge checks: short-outputs (<32 tokens) token-diff inspection, and long-sequence degradation trendline across prefix lengths
Manual review: sample 50 highest-priority regressions for human triage and annotate causes (tokenization, hallucination, truncated context)
Repro checks: reproducibility run on separate hardware (different GPU family) to catch kernel-selection instability
ci_checks: Static: linter and unit tests for metric-adapters; 95% coverage on adapter codepaths
Integration: nightly pipeline smoke run on eval fleet that validates report.json schema and gating logic
Performance: smoke dataset must finish within 45 minutes; fail CI if exceeded
Security: PII filter check must be enabled for datasets flagged as sensitive
Artifact: produced report.json must be uploaded to s3 and link returned in CI logs
rollout_strategy: Start with internal canary: run for internal-only profiles and collect feedback for 2 weeks
Beta: permit select Dedicated customers to opt-in to the auditable report for their private profiles
Gated: require metrics suite PASS for automated rollout to production model registry when profile is labeled auto-rollout-eligible
Fallback: if gating fails, automatic fallback to last-known-good quant profile (configurable TTL)
Monitoring: schedule post-rollout monitoring job at 1h, 6h, 24h with alerts to SRE if quality-index drops further
